# Study design

Each year is treated as one functional observation: the fertility rate is observed over age. The empirical comparison uses the same settings for Slovakia and France and contains exactly three forecasting methods:

1. **Benchmark:** FARFIMA(1,1,0), implemented as FAR(1) after fixing (d=1);
2. **Functional IC:** FARFIMA order selected by the proposed functional information criterion;
3. **CV:** FARFIMA order selected by expanding-window cross-validation.

The forecast study uses an expanding window, (h=1,\ldots,10), `p_max = q_max = 5`, `Npc = 1`, `B = 399`, and central 80% and 95% conformal intervals. Code is folded in the HTML report so that the figures and conclusions remain easy to read.

# Data and preprocessing

```{r data-functions}
repair_smooth <- function(raw, smooth) {
  raw <- as.matrix(raw)
  smooth <- as.matrix(smooth)
  smooth[!is.finite(smooth)] <- raw[!is.finite(smooth)]
  smooth
}

fertility_change <- function(x) {
  previous <- x[, -ncol(x), drop = FALSE]
  current <- x[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  denominator <- previous + current
  change <- 2 * (previous - current) / denominator
  change[denominator == 0] <- 0
  colnames(change) <- colnames(x)[-1]
  change
}

matrix_to_long <- function(x, country, data_type) {
  as.data.frame(x) |>
    rownames_to_column("age") |>
    pivot_longer(-age, names_to = "year", values_to = "rate") |>
    mutate(
      country = country,
      data_type = data_type,
      age = parse_number(age),
      year = parse_number(year)
    )
}

fer <- read_rds("Empirical Study/demog_list_asfr.rds")
country_codes <- c(Slovakia = "SVK", France = "FRATNP")

fertility_data <- imap(country_codes, function(code, country) {
  raw <- fer[[code]]$raw$rate[[paste0(code, "_ASFR")]] |> as.matrix()
  smooth <- fer[[code]]$smooth$rate[[paste0(code, "_ASFR")]] |> as.matrix()
  smooth <- repair_smooth(raw, smooth)

  list(
    raw = raw,
    smooth = smooth,
    smooth_change = fertility_change(smooth)
  )
})
```

The year-to-year change is

\[
C_t(u)=\frac{2\{F_{t-1}(u)-F_t(u)\}}
{F_{t-1}(u)+F_t(u)}.
\]

A positive value means that fertility at age (u) declined from the preceding year. Seven non-finite values in the supplied smoothed Slovakia matrix are replaced by the corresponding observed values.

# Integer-integration test

The sequential (V_0/V_1) test below follows the authors' official R code. It uses 26 Fourier basis functions, trapezoidal integration, a Bartlett long-run covariance estimate with bandwidth (lfloor T^{1/5}\rfloor), and the published 2.5% and 97.5% critical values 0.04467116 and 2.12588475.

The authors provide reproducibility scripts rather than an exported R-package function, so the short wrapper below reproduces those scripts directly.

```{r seo-shang-functions}
trapezoid_inner <- function(f, g, grid) {
  product <- f * g
  step <- grid[2] - grid[1]
  sum((head(product, -1) + tail(product, -1)) * step / 2)
}

fourier_scores <- function(x, n_basis = 26) {
  n_grid <- nrow(x)
  grid <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_grid)
  basis <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_grid, ncol = n_basis)

  for (j in seq_len(n_basis / 2)) {
    sine <- sqrt(2) * sin(2 * pi * j * grid)
    cosine <- sqrt(2) * cos(2 * pi * j * grid)
    basis[, 2 * j - 1] <- sine / sqrt(trapezoid_inner(sine, sine, grid))
    basis[, 2 * j] <- cosine / sqrt(trapezoid_inner(cosine, cosine, grid))
  }

  t(t(basis) %*% x * (grid[2] - grid[1]))
}

bartlett_long_run_sum <- function(x, bandwidth) {
  omega <- crossprod(x)

  if (bandwidth > 0) {
    lag_sum <- matrix(0, ncol(x), ncol(x))

    for (lag in seq_len(bandwidth)) {
      weight <- 1 - lag / bandwidth
      lag_sum <- lag_sum +
        weight * crossprod(
          x[seq_len(nrow(x) - lag), , drop = FALSE],
          x[(lag + 1):nrow(x), , drop = FALSE]
        )
    }

    omega <- omega + lag_sum + t(lag_sum)
  }

  omega
}

variance_ratio_statistic <- function(x, denominator, direction = NULL) {
  bandwidth <- floor(denominator^(1 / 5))
  partial_sums <- apply(x, 2, cumsum)
  partial_covariance <- crossprod(partial_sums) / denominator^2
  long_run_covariance <- bartlett_long_run_sum(x, bandwidth) / denominator

  if (is.null(direction)) {
    direction <- eigen(partial_covariance, symmetric = TRUE)$vectors[, 1]
  }

  numerator <- drop(crossprod(direction, partial_covariance %*% direction))
  denominator_value <- drop(crossprod(direction, long_run_covariance %*% direction))

  list(
    statistic = numerator / denominator_value,
    direction = direction,
    bandwidth = bandwidth
  )
}

seo_shang_integer_test <- function(x,
                                   lower = 0.04467116,
                                   upper = 2.12588475) {
  scores <- fourier_scores(x)

  v0_data <- sweep(scores[-1, , drop = FALSE], 2, scores[1, ], "-")
  v0 <- variance_ratio_statistic(v0_data, denominator = nrow(v0_data))

  v1_statistic <- NA_real_
  v1_decision <- "Not required"

  if (v0$statistic < lower) {
    conclusion <- "Fractional: d < 0"
  } else if (v0$statistic <= upper) {
    conclusion <- "I(0) is not rejected"
  } else {
    v1_data <- scores[-1, , drop = FALSE] - scores[-nrow(scores), , drop = FALSE]
    v1 <- variance_ratio_statistic(
      v1_data,
      denominator = nrow(scores),
      direction = v0$direction
    )

    v1_statistic <- v1$statistic
    v1_decision <- case_when(
      v1_statistic < lower ~ "Lower-tail rejection",
      v1_statistic <= upper ~ "Do not reject",
      TRUE ~ "Upper-tail rejection"
    )

    conclusion <- case_when(
      v1_statistic < lower ~ "Fractional: 0 < d < 1",
      v1_statistic <= upper ~ "I(1) is not rejected",
      TRUE ~ "Fractional: d > 1"
    )
  }

  tibble(
    V0 = v0$statistic,
    `V0 decision` = case_when(
      V0 < lower ~ "Lower-tail rejection",
      V0 <= upper ~ "Do not reject",
      TRUE ~ "Upper-tail rejection"
    ),
    V1 = v1_statistic,
    `V1 decision` = v1_decision,
    conclusion = conclusion,
    bandwidth = v0$bandwidth
  )
}
```

```{r seo-shang-results}
integer_test_results <- imap_dfr(fertility_data, function(x, country) {
  seo_shang_integer_test(x$smooth_change) |>
    mutate(Country = country, .before = 1)
})

integer_test_results |>
  dplyr::select(-bandwidth) |>
  kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Seo--Shang tests applied to the smoothed fertility-change series"
  )
```

For Slovakia, (V_0) rejects (I(0)) in the upper tail and (V_1) rejects (I(1)) in the lower tail, giving evidence for (0<d<1). For France, (V_0) rejects (I(0)), but (V_1) does not reject (I(1)).

The France result does **not** estimate (d=1). It says only that this sample does not contain enough evidence to reject the integer (I(1)) null. The LPWN procedure below is a separate semiparametric point estimator, so a fractional estimate and a failure to reject (I(1)) can occur together in a finite sample.

# Fractional differencing and dependence diagnostics

The full-sample estimate in this section is descriptive. The forecast experiment estimates (d) again from the initial training sample, so future test observations are not used to choose (d), (p), or (q).

```{r memory-estimation, fig.show='hide'}
memory_diagnostics <- imap(fertility_data, function(x, country) {
  centered <- sweep(
    x$smooth_change,
    1,
    rowMeans(x$smooth_change),
    "-"
  )

  set.seed(123)
  estimate <- estimate_d_BC_LPWN2(
    X = centered,
    m_const = 0.65,
    R_noise = 0,
    B = 399,
    memory_cov_type = "sample"
  )

  short_memory <- t(FCVAR::FracDiff(t(centered), d = estimate$d_BC_LPWN2))
  short_memory <- short_memory[, 21:ncol(short_memory), drop = FALSE]

  set.seed(123)
  identification <- fdaACF::FTS_identification(
    Y = t(short_memory),
    v = parse_number(rownames(centered)),
    nlags = min(10, ncol(short_memory) - 2),
    n_harm = NULL,
    ci = 0.95,
    estimation = "MC",
    figure = FALSE
  )

  list(
    d = estimate$d_BC_LPWN2,
    d_uncorrected = estimate$d_LPWN2,
    bootstrap_sd = estimate$sd_LPWN2,
    short_memory = short_memory,
    identification = identification
  )
})

memory_table <- imap_dfr(memory_diagnostics, function(x, country) {
  tibble(
    Country = country,
    `Uncorrected d` = x$d_uncorrected,
    `Bias-corrected d` = x$d,
    `Bootstrap SD` = x$bootstrap_sd
  )
})

memory_table |>
  kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Full-sample LPWN estimates used only for descriptive diagnostics"
  )
```

## Functional ACF and PACF after fractional differencing

The fACF and fPACF are computed with `fdaACF::FTS_identification()`. Following the package default, the FPCA dimension is the smallest number of components explaining at least 95% of the variance. Because these diagnostics are based on (L^2) norms, their values are non-negative; the dashed line is the package's upper 95% white-noise bound.

```{r facf-data}
facf_data <- imap_dfr(memory_diagnostics, function(x, country) {
  identification <- x$identification

  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      lag = seq_along(identification$rho_FACF),
      value = identification$rho_FACF,
      diagnostic = "fACF"
    ),
    tibble(
      lag = seq_along(identification$rho_FPACF),
      value = identification$rho_FPACF,
      diagnostic = "fPACF"
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      Country = country,
      bound = identification$Blueline
    )
})
```

```{r facf-plot, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
ggplot(facf_data, aes(lag, value)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = bound), linetype = 2, colour = "#D55E00") +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = lag, y = 0, yend = value), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_grid(Country ~ diagnostic, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(
    title = "Dependence after fractional differencing",
    subtitle = "Dashed line: upper 95% functional white-noise bound",
    x = "Lag",
    y = "Functional correlation"
  )
```

# Expanding-window forecast study

```{r run-models}
dir.create("Empirical Study/results", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

run_or_read_pipeline <- function(x, country, rerun = FALSE) {
  result_path <- file.path(
    "Empirical Study/results",
    paste0(tolower(country), "_fertility_change_forecast.rds")
  )

  if (!rerun && file.exists(result_path)) {
    return(readRDS(result_path))
  }

  result <- rolling_forecasting_pipeline_compact_order_method(
    X = x,
    h_max = 10,
    train_ratio = 0.6,
    valid_ratio = 0.2,
    alpha_set = c(0.2, 0.05),
    window_types = "expanding",
    p_max = 5,
    q_max = 5,
    Npc = 1,
    B = 399,
    far_pve = 0.95,
    fracdiff_trim = 20,
    seed = 123,
    far_benchmark_d = 1,
    order_selection_method = "both",
    cv_order_window_type = "expanding",
    memory_cov_type = "sample"
  )

  saveRDS(result, result_path)
  result
}

forecast_results <- imap(fertility_data, function(x, country) {
  run_or_read_pipeline(
    x = x$smooth_change,
    country = country,
    rerun = params$rerun_models
  )
})

validate_benchmark <- function(result) {
  benchmark <- result$error_detail |>
    filter(method == "far") |>
    arrange(order_selection_method, t0)

  ic <- benchmark |> filter(order_selection_method == "adaptive_ic")
  cv <- benchmark |> filter(order_selection_method == "cv_expanding")

  stopifnot(
    nrow(ic) == nrow(cv),
    identical(ic$t0, cv$t0),
    all(map2_lgl(ic$error, cv$error, ~ isTRUE(all.equal(.x, .y))))
  )
}

walk(forecast_results, validate_benchmark)
```

The benchmark appears internally under both order-selection runs, but those two benchmark forecasts are identical. It is therefore retained once and compared with one Functional IC forecast and one CV forecast.

## Selected models

```{r model-table}
selected_models <- imap_dfr(forecast_results, function(result, country) {
  selected <- result$model_summary |>
    filter(order_selection_method %in% c("adaptive_ic", "cv_expanding")) |>
    transmute(
      Country = country,
      Method = recode(
        order_selection_method,
        adaptive_ic = "Functional IC",
        cv_expanding = "CV"
      ),
      d = d_hat,
      p = p_est,
      q = q_est
    )

  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      Country = country,
      Method = "Benchmark (FARFIMA(1,1,0))",
      d = 1,
      p = 1L,
      q = 0L
    ),
    selected
  ) |>
    mutate(
      Method = as_method_factor(Method),
      Model = sprintf("FARFIMA(%d, %.4f, %d)", p, d, q)
    )
})

selected_models |>
  arrange(Country, Method) |>
  dplyr::select(Country, Method, Model) |>
  kable(caption = "Models fixed before evaluation on the test sample")
```

The estimated training-sample memory parameters are `r sprintf("%.4f", forecast_results$Slovakia$model_summary$d_hat[1])` for Slovakia and `r sprintf("%.4f", forecast_results$France$model_summary$d_hat[1])` for France. These are the approximately 0.8 and 0.4 values used in forecasting.

## Metrics

RMSE and MAE pool all ages and available test origins at each horizon. ECP is empirical coverage probability, CPD is its absolute deviation from nominal coverage, and Score is the mean interval score. WIS combines the point forecast with both the 80% and 95% interval scores. Smaller RMSE, MAE, CPD, Score, and WIS are better; ECP should be near its nominal level.

```{r metric-functions}
summarise_point_metrics <- function(result) {
  result$error_detail |>
    attach_method() |>
    mutate(horizon_metrics = map(error, function(error_matrix) {
      tibble(
        h = seq_len(ncol(error_matrix)),
        squared_error = colSums(error_matrix^2),
        absolute_error = colSums(abs(error_matrix)),
        n = nrow(error_matrix)
      )
    })) |>
    dplyr::select(Method, horizon_metrics) |>
    unnest(horizon_metrics) |>
    group_by(Method, h) |>
    summarise(
      RMSE = sqrt(sum(squared_error) / sum(n)),
      MAE = sum(absolute_error) / sum(n),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

summarise_interval_metrics <- function(result) {
  result$conformal_summary_detail |>
    attach_method() |>
    dplyr::select(Method, alpha, h, ECP, CPD, Score)
}

summarise_wis <- function(point, interval) {
  interval |>
    group_by(Method, h) |>
    summarise(
      K = n_distinct(alpha),
      weighted_interval = sum((alpha / 2) * Score),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    left_join(point |> dplyr::select(Method, h, MAE), by = c("Method", "h")) |>
    mutate(WIS = (0.5 * MAE + weighted_interval) / (K + 0.5)) |>
    dplyr::select(Method, h, WIS)
}

metric_results <- imap(forecast_results, function(result, country) {
  point <- summarise_point_metrics(result)
  interval <- summarise_interval_metrics(result)
  wis <- summarise_wis(point, interval)

  list(point = point, interval = interval, wis = wis)
})

point_metrics <- imap_dfr(metric_results, ~ mutate(.x$point, Country = .y, .before = 1))
interval_metrics <- imap_dfr(metric_results, ~ mutate(.x$interval, Country = .y, .before = 1))
wis_metrics <- imap_dfr(metric_results, ~ mutate(.x$wis, Country = .y, .before = 1))

point_ratios <- point_metrics |>
  left_join(
    point_metrics |>
      filter(Method == "Benchmark (FARFIMA(1,1,0))") |>
      dplyr::select(Country, h, benchmark_RMSE = RMSE, benchmark_MAE = MAE),
    by = c("Country", "h")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    `RMSE ratio` = RMSE / benchmark_RMSE,
    `MAE ratio` = MAE / benchmark_MAE
  )

interval_ratios <- interval_metrics |>
  left_join(
    interval_metrics |>
      filter(Method == "Benchmark (FARFIMA(1,1,0))") |>
      dplyr::select(Country, alpha, h, benchmark_Score = Score),
    by = c("Country", "alpha", "h")
  ) |>
  mutate(`Score ratio` = Score / benchmark_Score)

wis_ratios <- wis_metrics |>
  left_join(
    wis_metrics |>
      filter(Method == "Benchmark (FARFIMA(1,1,0))") |>
      dplyr::select(Country, h, benchmark_WIS = WIS),
    by = c("Country", "h")
  ) |>
  mutate(`WIS ratio` = WIS / benchmark_WIS)
```

### Point accuracy and WIS

The compact table reports raw values and benchmark ratios at horizons 1, 5, and 10. All ten horizons remain visible in the figures.

```{r point-wis-table}
point_ratios |>
  filter(h %in% c(1, 5, 10)) |>
  left_join(
    wis_ratios |> dplyr::select(Country, Method, h, WIS, `WIS ratio`),
    by = c("Country", "Method", "h")
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    Country,
    h,
    Method,
    RMSE,
    `RMSE ratio`,
    MAE,
    `MAE ratio`,
    WIS,
    `WIS ratio`
  ) |>
  arrange(Country, h, Method) |>
  kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Point accuracy and WIS at selected horizons"
  )
```

) +

  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ Country, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = method_palette,
    breaks = c("Functional IC", "CV")
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = method_shapes,
    breaks = c("Functional IC", "CV")
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = method_linetypes,
    breaks = c("Functional IC", "CV")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(
    title = "Weighted interval score relative to the benchmark",
    subtitle = "The horizontal line at one is the benchmark; WIS combines the point forecast and both intervals",
    x = "Forecast horizon h",
    y = "Ratio"
  )

# Point and interval forecasts

The final comparison uses the most recent test origin for which all ten forecast horizons are observed. The 80% and 95% bands are shown in separate figures to avoid overlapping the two coverage levels. Within every panel, the observed curve, all three point forecasts, and the bands for all three methods are compared directly.

```{r forecast-band-functions}
extract_forecast_bands <- function(result, x, country, alpha_show = c(0.20, 0.05)) {
  forecast_rows <- result$error_detail |>
    attach_method() |>
    mutate(n_horizons = map_int(error, ncol)) |>
    filter(n_horizons >= 10)

  latest_t0 <- forecast_rows |>
    distinct(t0, Method) |>
    dplyr::count(t0) |>
    filter(n == length(method_levels)) |>
    summarise(t0 = max(t0)) |>
    pull(t0)

  calibration_rows <- result$calibration_detail |>
    attach_method() |>
    filter(map_lgl(alpha, ~ any(abs(.x - alpha_show) < 1e-10)))

  map_dfr(method_levels, function(method_now) {
    error_matrix <- forecast_rows |>
      filter(t0 == latest_t0, Method == method_now) |>
      slice(1) |>
      pull(error) |>
      pluck(1)

    observed <- x[, latest_t0 + seq_len(10), drop = FALSE]
    forecast <- observed + error_matrix[, seq_len(10), drop = FALSE]

    calibration_rows |>
      filter(Method == method_now) |>
      arrange(desc(alpha)) |>
      pmap_dfr(function(alpha, gamma, zeta, ...) {
        map_dfr(seq_len(10), function(h) {
          half_width <- zeta[h] * as.numeric(gamma[[h]])
          tibble(
            Country = country,
            Method = as_method_factor(method_now),
            `Interval level` = factor(
              scales::percent(1 - alpha, accuracy = 1),
              levels = c("95%", "80%")
            ),
            h = h,
            panel = paste0("h = ", h),
            age = parse_number(rownames(x)),
            observed = observed[, h],
            forecast = forecast[, h],
            lower = forecast[, h] - half_width,
            upper = forecast[, h] + half_width
          )
        })
      })
    })
}

forecast_band_data <- imap_dfr(forecast_results, function(result, country) {
  extract_forecast_bands(
    result = result,
    x = fertility_data[[country]]$smooth_change,
    country = country
  )
}) |>
  mutate(
    panel = factor(
      panel,
      levels = paste0("h = ", 1:10)
    )
  )
```

```{r forecast-band-plots, results='asis', fig.width=13, fig.height=8.5}
plot_method_levels <- c("Benchmark", "Functional IC", "CV")
plot_method_palette <- c(
  "Benchmark" = "#7A5195",
  "Functional IC" = "#D55E00",
  "CV" = "#0072B2"
)
plot_method_linetypes <- c(
  "Benchmark" = "longdash",
  "Functional IC" = "solid",
  "CV" = "dotdash"
)

for (country_now in names(fertility_data)) {
  plot_data <- forecast_band_data |>
    filter(Country == country_now) |>
    mutate(
      `Plot method` = recode(
        as.character(Method),
        `Benchmark (FARFIMA(1,1,0))` = "Benchmark"
      ),
      `Plot method` = factor(`Plot method`, levels = plot_method_levels)
    )

  observed_data <- plot_data |>
    distinct(panel, h, age, observed)

  point_data <- plot_data |>
    distinct(panel, h, age, `Plot method`, forecast)

  for (interval_now in c("80%", "95%")) {
    band_data <- plot_data |>
      filter(`Interval level` == interval_now)

    forecast_plot <- ggplot() +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = band_data,
        aes(
          x = age,
          ymin = lower,
          ymax = upper,
          fill = `Plot method`,
          group = `Plot method`
        ),
        alpha = 0.14,
        colour = NA
      ) +
      geom_line(
        data = observed_data,
        aes(age, observed),
        colour = "#111111",
        linewidth = 1.2
      ) +
      geom_line(
        data = point_data,
        aes(
          age,
          forecast,
          colour = `Plot method`,
          linetype = `Plot method`,
          group = `Plot method`
        ),
        linewidth = 1
      ) +
      facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 5, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_colour_manual(
        name = "Point forecast",
        values = plot_method_palette,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      scale_linetype_manual(
        name = "Point forecast",
        values = plot_method_linetypes,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(
        name = paste(interval_now, "prediction band"),
        values = plot_method_palette,
        drop = FALSE
      ) +
      guides(
        colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.2)),
        linetype = guide_legend(order = 1),
        fill = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(alpha = 0.18))
      ) +
      labs(
        title = paste(country_now, interval_now, "fertility-change forecasts"),
        subtitle = "Observed: black solid line; benchmark: purple long-dashed line",
        x = "Age",
        y = "Fertility-rate change"
      ) +
      theme(
        legend.box = "vertical",
        plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 16)
      )

    print(forecast_plot)
  }
}
```

# Interpretation notes

- The Seo--Shang test and LPWN estimator answer different questions. “(I(1)) is not rejected” is not an estimate of (d=1), so it should not replace the reported LPWN estimate.
- A ratio below one favours Functional IC or CV over the FARFIMA(1,1,0) benchmark. The benchmark ratio is one by construction.
- WIS is one proper score formed jointly from the point forecast and the two central intervals. The 80% and 95% interval scores are also reported separately.
- This is an out-of-sample empirical comparison over rolling forecast origins, not a Monte Carlo simulation distribution.

- Seo, W.-K. and Shang, H. L. (2026), [Testing for integer integration in functional time series](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23960), and the authors' [official R implementation](https://github.com/wonkiseo86/Testing_Integer_Integration).
- Mestre, G., Portela, J., Rice, G., Muñoz San Roque, A. and Alonso, E. (2021), [Functional time series model identification and diagnosis by means of auto- and partial autocorrelation analysis](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csda.2020.107108). The implementation used here is in the [`fdaACF` CRAN package](https://cran.r-project.org/package=fdaACF).
- Hyndman, R. J. and Shang, H. L. (2010), [Rainbow plots, bagplots, and boxplots for functional data](https://robjhyndman.com/publications/rainbow-fda/).
- Paparoditis, E. and Shang, H. L. (2021), [Bootstrap prediction bands for functional time series](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.03971).
